newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait to shed holdings in local industrial bank.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait to shed holdings in local industrial bank.

text.p: Kuwait plans to sell most of its shares in the Industrial Bank of Kuwait (IBK) in a two-stage privatisation bid, the Kuwait News Agency said on Tuesday.

The Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA), the state investment arm, will sell 30 million of its 100 million IBK shares in a public auction in November and another 60 million in a public subscription at a later stage, said the agency.
KIA owns 32 percent of IBK, which acts as a conduit for soft government loans to industry. Other state bodies are also shareholders in IBK.
KIA has set the starting price for the auction at 410 fils ($1.37). The price for the subscription is due to be set at a later stage. There are 1,000 fils to the dinar.

The sale is part of Kuwait's plan to shed state holdings in about 60 local firms and public services such as electricity, water and telecommunications. The plan, announced after the 1991 Gulf War, is supervised by KIA.
